newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt keen to cap spending medium term.
newsitem.headline: French govt keen to cap spending medium term.

text.p: French government officials said on Thursday there was no specific plan for a five-year spending freeze but a general political will existed to rein in government spending in the medium term.

Conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe has sent a letter to all ministries saying spending next year must be capped at 1996 levels for the second year running in a continuation of the centre-right government's austerity policy.

The daily Le Figaro on Thursday cited a government source saying renewal of this freeze was the "norm fixed for the (five-year) term of the legislature". France has a parliamentary election in two rounds on May 25 and June 1.
"There is no plan over five years," said a Finance Ministry official. "But there is a global political determination to see the government's operating deficit reduced," the official said.
Another official said: "We are are heading for a policy of stabilising public spending in the medium term".
Both officials underlined that Juppe's letter concerning a spending freeze for 1998 -- the letter was made public on Thursday -- was for that year, and that year only.
Budget-capping measures were only carried out year-by-year, said one of the officials.
